$comment: Source of truth for which MCP servers this registry exposes. Edit, then re-run scripts/build.sh. Entries default to source "upstream"; "local" publishes a blob from local/<name>/<version>.json instead — see README.md.

servers.name: com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server
servers.notes: Atlassian Rovo remote MCP server (Jira, Confluence, Loom). `latest` is 2.0.0, whose default remote is https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp. 1.1.2 stays pinned so the v1 remotes remain resolvable through the v1→v2 transition; Atlassian begins serving v2 tools to v1 connections on 2027-03-01.

servers.name: net.cerebras.sec/atlassian
servers.notes: Same Atlassian service as the com.atlassian entry above, but routed through Runlayer proxy f06f1af5 so Copilot traffic is policed and audited. Published alongside rather than replacing it: Copilot enforces on server ID, so retiring com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server would cut off anyone already installed under that ID. Of Runlayer's four Atlassian servers this is the only one fit for interactive use — faad5da6 and 2ccdb53c front v1/mcp, whose sign-in Copilot can't complete over Remote-SSH, and 1bf125a8 and 2ccdb53c inject a static API key, so every user would share one identity in the audit log.

servers.name: net.cerebras.sec/slack
servers.notes: Slack official remote MCP server via Runlayer proxy a4838591. Not in the upstream registry, so the blob is hand-authored. Remote points at the proxy, not mcp.slack.com, to keep Copilot under Runlayer policy and audit.
